config.title: Data Service

intro.title: Data Service
intro.body: In this lesson, you'll build a data service that manages and provides data to multiple components in an Angular application. You'll learn about Angular services, which are singleton classes that encapsulate business logic and data operations, keeping your components clean and focused on presentation. The lesson covers creating an injectable service using the @Injectable decorator, implementing methods to retrieve and manipulate data, and using Angular's dependency injection system to share the service across components. You'll work with TypeScript classes, observables for handling asynchronous data, and the Angular CLI to generate service files. By the end, you'll understand how services promote code reusability and separation of concerns in Angular applications.
intro.usecase: Data services are essential in Angular applications for managing and sharing data across components, commonly seen in e-commerce platforms that fetch product catalogs, user profiles, and shopping cart data from APIs. Social media dashboards use data services to retrieve posts, user interactions, and analytics from multiple endpoints while keeping components synchronized. Banking applications rely on data services to securely fetch account balances, transaction histories, and user preferences, ensuring consistent data flow between different views like account summaries, transaction lists, and profile settings. This pattern centralizes API communication logic, making applications more maintainable and enabling efficient data caching and error handling across the entire application.

objectives: Implement a service class with the @Injectable decorator to encapsulate data logic
Configure HTTP client methods to fetch data from external APIs
Construct observable streams to handle asynchronous data operations
Integrate the data service into components through dependency injection
Apply error handling mechanisms for failed data requests
Manipulate retrieved data using RxJS operators before displaying in templates
Initialize service subscriptions within component lifecycle hooks

steps.title: Import HttpClient and Injectable
steps.instruction: Import HttpClient from '@angular/common/http' and Injectable from '@angular/core'
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both HttpClient and Injectable from their respective Angular modules
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing multiple Angular modules
import { Component, OnInit } from '@angular/core';

seedCode.App.tsx: // Import the necessary Angular modules here

steps.expectedOutcome: HttpClient and Injectable are imported and ready to be used in the data service
successCriteria: HttpClient is imported from '@angular/common/http' and Injectable is imported from '@angular/core'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one of the modules, but make sure to include both HttpClient from '@angular/common/http' and Injectable from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your import statements. You need to import HttpClient from '@angular/common/http' and Injectable from '@angular/core' using the correct syntax.

steps.title: Create the data service class
steps.instruction: Create a DataService class and apply the @Injectable decorator to make it available for dependency injection.
steps.hint: Use the @Injectable() decorator above the class definition, then create the class with the export keyword.
steps.expectedOutcome: A DataService class is created with the @Injectable decorator, making it ready to be used as a service in Angular applications.
successCriteria: DataService class is defined with @Injectable decorator and export keyword
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have both the @Injectable() decorator and the DataService class definition with the export keyword.
steps.feedbackWrong: create a class named DataService with the @Injectable() decorator above it and the export keyword before the class.

steps.title: Inject HttpClient into the service constructor
steps.instruction: Add a constructor to the DataService class that injects HttpClient as a private parameter.
steps.hint: Use dependency injection by creating a constructor with 'private http: HttpClient' as a parameter.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: injecting a service into a constructor
constructor(private userService: UserService) {}
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataService class will have a constructor that accepts HttpClient through dependency injection, making it available throughout the service.
successCriteria: A constructor is added to DataService that injects HttpClient as a private parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your constructor parameter is marked as private and has the correct type annotation for HttpClient.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor should inject HttpClient as a private parameter. Use the syntax: constructor(private http: HttpClient) {}

steps.title: Define the API endpoint URL
steps.instruction: Create a private property named apiUrl to store the API endpoint URL string
steps.hint: Add a private property inside the class to hold the base URL for your API calls. Use a realistic URL like 'https://api.example.com/data'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: private property in a class
private baseUrl = 'https://api.myapp.com/users';
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataService class will have a private property that stores the API endpoint URL for making HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A private property named apiUrl is defined with a string value containing an API endpoint URL
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your property is private and contains a valid URL string.
steps.feedbackWrong: add a private property named apiUrl with a string value containing an API endpoint URL inside the DataService class.

steps.title: Create a method to fetch all data
steps.instruction: Add a getData method inside the DataService class that uses this.http.get to make a GET request to the API endpoint and return the Observable
steps.hint: Create a public method that calls this.http.get() with the apiUrl and returns the result. The method should return an Observable.
steps.expectedOutcome: A getData method is added to the DataService class that uses HttpClient.get to fetch data from the API endpoint
successCriteria: The DataService class contains a getData method that uses this.http.get with the apiUrl and returns an Observable
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your getData method uses this.http.get() with the apiUrl and returns the Observable result.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getData method should use this.http.get() to make a GET request to this.apiUrl and return the Observable. Check that you're calling the http.get method correctly.

steps.title: Create a method to fetch data by ID
steps.instruction: Add a getDataById method to the DataService class that accepts an id parameter and returns an HTTP GET request to fetch a specific user by ID
steps.hint: Create a method that takes an id parameter and uses this.http.get() with the API URL followed by the ID
steps.expectedOutcome: A getDataById method is added that accepts an id parameter and makes an HTTP GET request to fetch a specific user
successCriteria: The getDataById method is defined with an id parameter and returns this.http.get() with the appropriate URL
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your method accepts an id parameter and uses it in the URL path.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method needs to accept an id parameter and use this.http.get() with the URL that includes the ID.

steps.title: Create a method to post new data
steps.instruction: Add a createData method that accepts a data parameter and uses HttpClient.post to send it to the API endpoint
steps.hint: Use this.http.post() with the apiUrl and the data parameter. The method should return the observable from the HTTP call.
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataService class will have a createData method that accepts data and makes a POST request to create new data
successCriteria: A createData method is defined that accepts a parameter and uses this.http.post with the apiUrl
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your createData method accepts a data parameter and uses this.http.post with the apiUrl.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createData method should accept a data parameter and use this.http.post(this.apiUrl, data) to send the data to the API.

steps.title: Create a method to update existing data
steps.instruction: Add an updateData method that takes an id and data parameter and uses the HttpClient put method to update existing data at the API endpoint
steps.hint: Use this.http.put() with the URL including the id parameter and pass the data as the second argument
steps.expectedOutcome: The service should have an updateData method that accepts id and data parameters and returns an HTTP PUT request observable
successCriteria: updateData method is defined with id and data parameters and uses this.http.put with the correct URL structure
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your updateData method takes both id and data parameters and uses the put method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateData method should use this.http.put() with the URL containing the id parameter and the data to update.

steps.title: Create a method to delete data
steps.instruction: Add a deleteData method that takes an id parameter and uses HttpClient.delete to remove data by ID
steps.hint: Use this.http.delete() with the API URL and the ID parameter to create a DELETE request
steps.expectedOutcome: A deleteData method is added that accepts an id parameter and returns an HTTP DELETE request
successCriteria: The deleteData method is defined with an id parameter and uses this.http.delete with the correct URL pattern
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your deleteData method takes an id parameter and uses this.http.delete with the correct URL.
steps.feedbackWrong: The deleteData method should take an id parameter and use this.http.delete() with the API URL and ID.

steps.title: Add error handling to the service methods
steps.instruction: Import the catchError operator from 'rxjs/operators' and add error handling to the getData method using catchError
steps.hint: Import catchError at the top, then pipe the HTTP request through catchError to handle any potential errors. You can use throwError from 'rxjs' to re-throw the error after logging it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The service will have catchError imported and used in the getData method to handle HTTP errors gracefully
successCriteria: catchError and throwError are imported from RxJS, and the getData method uses pipe() with catchError to handle errors
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you've imported both catchError from 'rxjs/operators' and throwError from 'rxjs', then used pipe() with catchError in the getData method.
steps.feedbackWrong: import the necessary RxJS operators and add error handling to the getData method using pipe() and catchError.

steps.title: Register the service in the module providers
steps.instruction: Add the DataService to the providers array in the app module to make it available for dependency injection throughout the application
steps.hint: Import DataService at the top of the module file, then add it to the providers array in the @NgModule decorator
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataService is imported and added to the providers array, making it available for dependency injection
successCriteria: DataService is imported and included in the providers array of the NgModule decorator
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to both import DataService at the top and add it to the providers array.
steps.feedbackWrong: import DataService and add it to the providers array in the @NgModule decorator to register it for dependency injection.

steps.title: Inject and use the service in a component
steps.instruction: Import DataService in the AppComponent and inject it into the constructor
steps.hint: Use the import statement at the top of the file and add DataService as a parameter to the constructor with proper access modifier
steps.expectedOutcome: DataService is imported and injected into the AppComponent constructor
successCriteria: DataService is imported from the data service file and injected as a private parameter in the constructor
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you have both the import statement and the constructor parameter with the private access modifier.
steps.feedbackWrong: add an import statement for DataService and inject it into the constructor as a private parameter. Check the syntax for constructor injection in Angular.
